title: brew relocates and re-signs a keg's Mach-O files after the install body hashes them, so doctor fails a clean keg (blocks 0326 in Gtools)
body:
Found by Gtools (gtools-vc, from gtools-dc's measurement in Gtools issue 0129), 2026-11-23 04:22Z by date -u.

On macOS, brew relocates and ad-hoc re-signs a keg's precompiled native objects (Gtools' exqlite and mdex NIFs) after the install body has hashed them, so the manifest row fails `doctor` on a keg nobody touched. devbin's T8 install body (`bin/devbin install --prefix libexec --managed-by brew`) hashes at that same moment, and devbin has no re-hash or relocation handling: a grep of `bin/.devbin/lib` and `docs/` finds none. Gtools' formula works around it today by re-hashing in `post_install`, which brew has deprecated.

So issue 0326's adoption in Gtools (Gtools I7bd0048), as filed, regresses Gtools 0129 on every macOS brew install. It blocks that adoption, and any other estate whose keg holds Mach-O files brew rewrites.

The two shapes gtools-dc offers, both in devbin:

- a re-hash step that `post_install_steps` calls, after brew's relocation; or
- `doctor` reading a brew keg's Mach-O files without their load commands and code signature.

The shape is chosen in devbin-cc's Gtools plan under 0326, and lands in devbin before Gtools' adoption.


Resolution (cc, 2026-11-23 17:17Z by date -u): fixed by the re-hash shape, landed at 534fd421. Every formula devbin renders, source mode and assets mode, now ends with a `post_install_steps` block written after the template's install. Homebrew runs it after it has relocated and re-signed the keg, at a source install's end and at a bottle's pour. It holds one `run` step: /bin/sh over libexec and install.manifest, keeping the manifest's `#` lines and order and hashing each listed file again with the tool lib/helpers' SHA256_SH chooses. A manifest naming a missing file, holding a line that is no file's, or listing no file is left as it was, and the step fails. A template holding its own post_install or post_install_steps is refused. The doctor shape was not taken: a re-hashed manifest is true for every reader, and a tool's own doctor is the only one a keg without a checkout has. The same unit takes the assets install body's sum out of its interpolation, which brew 7.0.15's Homebrew/SimpleInterpolation refused. Proof at the Desk (01M84P9Z0E85F5MCM1TT5ZTVYP): red at the base, formula.bats whole under BSD and GNU, test scans and check lint, all green. A real brew install of a rendered formula is T10's brew leg. Gtools' adoption (I7bd0048) may now drop its own post_install re-hash.
